name: Barone Fistula Catheter Trial
question: Is removing the bladder catheter 7 days after repair of a simple female genital fistula noninferior to removal at 14 days for repair breakdown?

design.population: Women at eight hospitals in eight African countries with a surgeon-judged simple genital fistula that was closed on dye test at the end of surgery and still closed 7 days after repair.
design.description: Multicenter open-label noninferiority randomized trial across eight African hospitals

verdictNote: Upper confidence limit 4.5 points against a 10-point margin; open-label, simple fistulas closed at day 7 only.
takeaway: In women with a simple fistula closed 7 days after repair, removing the bladder catheter at 7 days was noninferior to 14 days: breakdown from 8 days after catheter removal to 3 months occurred in 10/250 (4.0%) versus 8/251 (3.2%), within a 10-point margin.

reports.label: Randomized noninferiority report
reports.citation: Barone MA, Widmer M, Arrowsmith S, et al. Breakdown of simple female genital fistula repair after 7 day versus 14 day postoperative bladder catheterisation: a randomised, controlled, open-label, non-inferiority trial. *Lancet.* 2015;386(9988):56-62. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(14)62337-0
reports.followUp: 3 months after surgery (primary window from 8 days after catheter removal)

results.measure: Dye-test-defined repair breakdown from 8 days after catheter removal to 3 months after surgery, per-protocol; risk difference in percentage points (7-day minus 14-day); noninferiority margin 10 points
results.note: Relative risk 1.3 (95% CI 0.5 to 3.1). The upper confidence limit of 4.5 points was below the 10-point margin. Only one analysis was done, in the per-protocol population (one ineligible participant excluded).

results.endpoint: Repair breakdown, catheter removal to 3 months
results.measure: Dye-test-defined breakdown from catheter removal to 3 months after surgery; risk difference in percentage points (7-day minus 14-day)
results.note: Relative risk 1.2 (95% CI 0.7 to 2.1). Includes breakdowns found at the dye test 7 days after catheter removal.

results.endpoint: Repair breakdown, catheter removal to 7 days after removal
results.measure: Dye-test-defined breakdown at the dye test 7 days after catheter removal; risk difference in percentage points (7-day minus 14-day)
results.note: Relative risk 1.1 (95% CI 0.5 to 2.3). Reported separately by the authors and not prespecified.

results.measure: Residual incontinence after fistula closure at the 3-month visit; risk difference in percentage points (7-day minus 14-day)
results.note: Relative risk 1.5 (95% CI 0.5 to 4.2). Based on the surgeon's history and examination, without urodynamic studies. Diagnoses among the affected women: stress 11, overflow 2, urge 2.

results.measure: Primary outcome with missing observations imputed as a four-fold breakdown proportion in the 11 lost to follow-up in the 7-day group and a 99% reduction in the 11 lost in the 14-day group; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Percentages are rounded as reported. Nine scenarios were examined; this was the worst. The upper limit stayed below the 10-point margin.

harms.label: Urinary retention during hospital stay
harms.note: Risk difference 2.3 points (95% CI -3.3 to 8.0). After catheter removal there were 100 retention episodes (54 in the 7-day group, 46 in the 14-day group) in 56 participants; 48/54 (88.9%) and 42/46 (91.3%) of the episodes were treated successfully with intermittent catheterization.

harms.label: Infection possibly related to treatment
harms.note: Risk difference -3.0 points (95% CI -7.0 to 0.9). Ten urinary tract infections (6 versus 4), four vaginal infections (all in the 14-day group), five surgical wound infections (2 versus 3) and five other infections (all in the 14-day group); all mild or moderate and treated with antibiotics.

harms.label: Febrile episode (above 38 C) possibly related to treatment
Catheter blockage
harms.note: Risk difference -2.3 points (95% CI -5.6 to 0.8). Blockages were resolved in roughly equal numbers by flushing the catheter and drainage tube or by replacing the catheter.

harms.label: Extended hospital stay for a possibly treatment-related medical reason
harms.note: Risk difference 1.5 points (95% CI -0.7 to 3.7); relative risk 5.0 (95% CI 0.6 to 42.7). Defined as a stay beyond 1 week after initial catheter removal.

harms.label: Intraoperative complications (before randomization)
harms.note: Recorded at the index operation, before the 7-day and 14-day catheter assignment.

delivery.label: Timing of catheter removal

values.exp: Postoperative day 7, on the day of randomization

delivery.note: Participants stayed at the facility for 7 days after catheter removal; the dye test was done 7 days after removal (postoperative day 14 versus day 21).

delivery.label: Assessed for eligibility and randomized
delivery.note: 483 were ineligible, including 381 with a non-simple fistula at postsurgery screening, 23 with a positive dye test after surgery and 29 with a positive dye test at the randomization screen.

delivery.label: Lost to follow-up
delivery.note: 250 and 251 participants were analysed; one randomized participant in the 14-day group was ineligible (positive postsurgery dye test) and excluded from all analyses.

delivery.label: Primary outcome detected before the 3-month visit
delivery.note: Women who returned after discharge with urine leakage and had a positive dye test.

delivery.label: Empirical postoperative antibiotics before randomization
delivery.note: After randomization no participant received prophylactic antibiotics.

delivery.label: Counselled to do pelvic floor exercises before randomization
delivery.note: Bladder training was given to 25 (10%) in each group before randomization and to none afterward.

delivery.label: Postrandomization care
delivery.value: Standardized: daily perineal and vaginal care, walking and free fluids encouraged, no prophylactic antibiotics or anthelmintics, no bladder training, catheter blockage monitored and treated

delivery.label: Management of urinary retention
delivery.value: Postvoid residual measured by urethral catheter 1, 3 and 7 days after catheter removal; retention was a residual above 50% of the voided volume and was managed with intermittent catheterization at least 3 times daily until the residual was below 50% of the voided volume on two consecutive occasions

delivery.label: Definition of a simple fistula
delivery.value: Judged by the operating surgeon at the end of surgery with no fixed definition; 17 surgeons classified fistula drawings with a kappa of 0.55

delivery.label: Women with multiple fistulas randomized before the exclusion criterion
delivery.note: Multiple fistula became an exclusion criterion on July 31, 2012; these 12 women (2% of participants) are listed by the authors as a limitation.

delivery.label: Planned sample size
delivery.value: 507 women (177 per arm before inflation for loss to follow-up and protocol violations)
delivery.note: Assumed 13% breakdown in the 14-day group, 10% margin, one-sided alpha 0.025, power 80%.

delivery.label: Fistula location, juxtaurethral
delivery.note: More than one location or type was possible per participant.

delivery.label: Moderate or severe scarring
delivery.note: Moderate 35 and severe 1 in the 7-day group; moderate 29 and severe 4 in the 14-day group.

delivery.label: Leakage started after delivery of a baby
